name: Asia Mall
whatItIs: Two-story, about 116,000-square-foot pan-Asian mall opened late 2022, anchored by an Asian grocery; Chinese, Vietnamese and Korean tenants.
evidence: Mpls.St.Paul Magazine (Feb. 10, 2026) lists the Chinese Community Center's Lunar New Year celebration at Asia Mall on Feb. 15, 2026; Chinese Community Center's own 2026 site gives its address as Suite 208 in the mall. Ownership is not Chinese-specific (pan-Asian).

name: Asia Village
whatItIs: Second Asian-themed complex planned by Asia Mall's owners in a 100,000-square-foot building connected to Northtown Mall, with a large Asian grocery.
evidence: May 2024 announcement targeted late 2025 or early 2026 opening; no opened page confirms it has opened.

name: Keefer Court
neighborhoodOrCity: Eden Prairie (Asia Mall); formerly West Bank, Minneapolis
whatItIs: Chinese bakery founded by Sunny and Paulina Kwan in 1983 (began as a fortune cookie business); closed Dec. 2022; reopened March 2024 at Asia Mall under owners Michael Bui, Mai Bui and Peter Do.
evidence: MPR News, March 15, 2024, reports the reopening; no 2025 or 2026 page opened confirms it is still operating.

name: United Noodles
whatItIs: Family-owned Asian grocery, 'Minnesota's Asian Market Since 1972,' selling noodles, sauces, produce, hot pot ingredients and kitchenware.
evidence: Own site lists store hours for Minneapolis and Woodbury, copyright 2026. Ownership heritage is not stated on the page.

name: Rainbow Chinese Restaurant
neighborhoodOrCity: Whittier / Eat Street, Minneapolis (2739 Nicollet Ave. S.)
whatItIs: Chef Tammy Wong's restaurant, opened when she was 23 and run for more than 36 years; Wong was born in the Chinese quarter of Saigon.
evidence: Own site lists hours Wednesday to Sunday; Mpls.St.Paul Magazine (Feb. 10, 2026) lists a free Family Meal there on Feb. 18, 2026.

name: Shuang Cheng Restaurant
whatItIs: Cantonese restaurant near the University of Minnesota, known for seafood and Peking duck.
evidence: Named in Mpls.St.Paul Magazine and Meet Minneapolis Lunar New Year guides, February 2026, offering a 2026 Peking duck special. Own site could not be opened.

name: Tea House Chinese Restaurant
whatItIs: Regional Chinese restaurant serving Sichuan and Anhui specialties, including whole fish.
evidence: Named in Meet Minneapolis and Mpls.St.Paul Magazine Lunar New Year guides, February 2026.

name: Legendary Spice
neighborhoodOrCity: Dinkytown, Minneapolis; also opened at Asia Mall in 2022
whatItIs: Chinese restaurant known for spicy dishes such as dry pot prawns and hot and sour beef; offered a $188 Chinese New Year family feast in 2026.
evidence: Meet Minneapolis 2026 Lunar New Year page lists its 2026 Chinese New Year special for the Dinkytown location; Sahan Journal (Nov. 2022) listed it among Asia Mall's opening tenants. Asia Mall location not separately confirmed.

name: Yangtze Restaurant
whatItIs: Restaurant serving Hunan, Sichuan, Mandarin and Cantonese dishes, with weekend dim sum 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
evidence: Named in Meet Minneapolis and Mpls.St.Paul Magazine Lunar New Year guides, February 2026.

name: JUN Szechuan Kitchen
neighborhoodOrCity: North Loop, Minneapolis (730 N. Washington Ave., #140)
whatItIs: Sichuan restaurant with Shandong-style dumplings, run by Shandong-born chef Jessie Wong and her son Jack, who opened Szechuan in Roseville in 2009.
evidence: Mpls.St.Paul Magazine, Feb. 10, 2026, lists its Lunar New Year noodles and dumplings; own site could not be opened.

name: Szechuan (Roseville)
whatItIs: Sichuan restaurant opened in 2009 by Jessie and Jack Wong, the owners of JUN.
evidence: Mentioned only as the owners' earlier restaurant on the North Loop directory page; no current page opened.

name: Peking Garden
neighborhoodOrCity: University Avenue, St. Paul (Little Mekong area)
whatItIs: Cantonese restaurant since 1991, now in its third location in the former Mai Village space; live seafood and hot pot.
evidence: Hosted the fifth annual Twin Cities Dumpling Feast on Feb. 25, 2026 (Minnesota Monthly and Mpls.St.Paul Magazine, Feb. 10, 2026).

name: Master Noodle
whatItIs: Restaurant known for hand-pulled biang biang noodles and Sichuan dishes.
evidence: Listed in Visit Saint Paul's undated Chinese restaurants guide (site copyright 2026); no dated current page opened.

name: Kim's Chow Mein
whatItIs: Small, long-running neighborhood Chinese-American restaurant.
evidence: Listed in Visit Saint Paul's undated guide only.

name: Golden Chow Mein
whatItIs: Neighborhood Cantonese takeout restaurant of about three decades.
evidence: Listed in Visit Saint Paul's undated guide only.

name: Little Szechuan Hot Pot
whatItIs: Sichuan hot pot restaurant.
evidence: Listed in Visit Saint Paul's undated guide only.

name: Grand Szechuan
whatItIs: Sichuan restaurant serving since 2008, led by Chef Luo.
evidence: Own site with current dine-in and take-out menus, address and ordering links.

name: Mandarin Kitchen
whatItIs: Long-known Twin Cities dim sum restaurant.
evidence: The domain now shows a page titled 'Welcome to Mr. Ping's Noodles'; city tourism page blocked; no current confirmation.

name: Home Taste
whatItIs: Chinese restaurant listed among Asia Mall's opening tenants.
evidence: Only source is Sahan Journal, Nov. 1, 2022.

name: Leeann Chin
whatItIs: Chinese-American fast-casual chain founded by Leeann Chin, who opened her first restaurant in Minnetonka in 1980.
evidence: Own site with locations and online ordering, copyright 2026. The founder died in 2010 and the business has been sold more than once.

name: David Fong's
neighborhoodOrCity: Bloomington (Lyndale Ave. S. at W. 94th St.)
whatItIs: Cantonese-American restaurant opened by David Sr. and Helen Fong in 1958 as Fong's Chow Mein.
evidence: FOX 9 reported it would close at the end of August 2022 after 64 years as Edward Fong retired.

name: Fong family restaurants, Prior Lake and Savage
whatItIs: Locations owned by other Fong siblings.
evidence: FOX 9 (2022) said they would remain open; no current page opened.

name: Dragon Cafe Chinese Restaurant
whatItIs: Family restaurant bought by a Guangdong immigrant family in 1986, later run by an older daughter; three generations have worked there.
evidence: Shakopee Heritage Society profile is undated; no current page opened.

name: Chinese Community Center
whatItIs: Nonprofit founded by grassroots organizers; social services, health services, youth programs, Mandarin and Cantonese tutoring, support for minority-owned businesses, and a large Lunar New Year festival.
evidence: Own site copyright 2026 with posts dated Sept. and Oct. 2026.

name: Chinese American Association of Minnesota (CAAM)
whatItIs: State's oldest Chinese American organization (1951; incorporated 1967): Chinese Dance Theater, language school, scholarships, community meals.
evidence: Posts dated Dec. 2025 and July 1, 2026, report 2025 and 2026 events.

name: Chinese Social Service Center
whatItIs: Community center for Chinese Americans: immigrant counseling, ESL and citizenship classes, benefits applications, translation, home care and PCA services, senior program.
evidence: United Way 211 listing last assured Nov. 20, 2025.

name: Twin Cities Chinese Language School
whatItIs: Nonprofit Chinese school founded in 1976 (CAAM gives January 1975) teaching traditional characters, Zhuyin and Pinyin.
evidence: Own site with current programs, staff and registration; CAAM language school page lists principals through 2025.

name: Chinese Chamber of Commerce (Minnesota)
whatItIs: Business group formed in the early 1970s when merchants split from CAAM.
evidence: Known only from CAAM's history page; no current organization page found.

name: News & Views (CAAM newsletter)
whatItIs: English and Chinese newsletter of CAAM, listed from 1994.
evidence: MNHS library guide lists it as '[1994]-current' but gives no recent issue.
